The Random block generates a random number within a range each time is it used.



There are many interesting way to use random numbers. Below are just some examples:



Let's test the Random block out. Create a code that repeatedly places an "O" at a random position on the LCD at 0.1 second interval as shown below. 
Note that it seems to slow down because it could be placing the "O" at a spot that is already filled. The program will keep running even when the display is fully filled.

Neuroinclusive design focuses on creating environments and technologies that support neurodivergent individuals, such as those with ADHD or autism. It is gaining attention as awareness and diagnoses of neurodevelopmental conditions continue to rise.

We can be creative in how we use the blocks. In the example below, connecting the Ultrasonic block to the LCD column sets the column to match the obstacle's distance. If the distance is greater than 15 (exceeds column size), it is not displayed.



Some workplaces offer a Quiet Room for neurodivergent staff to regulate and calm themselves when needed. 


The Lab needs your help coding its new Quiet Room, which lets users enter and relax by randomly painting a digital display. A simple flow diagram outlines the program.
